newsitem.title: UK: Investors reject Cantrade compensation offer.
newsitem.headline: Investors reject Cantrade compensation offer.

text.p: A Jersey lawyer acting for investors who have allegedly suffered losses as a result of foreign exchange trading effected through Cantrade Private Bank, a unit of UBS, has rejected a compensation offer.

On Monday, UBS said it was offering to compensate TTS International SA investors for the losses on trades effected through Cantrade by UK-based independent foreign exchange trader Robert Young and his companies.
"The essential proposal is that those investors will have their trading losses repaid by Cantrade with appropriate interest," UBS said.

Cantrade, a wholly owned subsidiary of Union Bank of Switzerland, did not disclose the terms of the offer but it is thought to have been around the $15 million mark when interest is taken into account.

But, in a statement, Philip Senel, acting for TTS and other parties who claim to have lost $27 million, said the offer was "pathtically inadequate" and "far too late to offer any meaningful comfort to any of the parties involved,"
Sinel said that the offer also had conditions attached which were "completely unacceptable and impracticable."
Last October, police in the British Channel island of Jersey said they had charged Cantrade and one of its officers, Peter Stoneman, under Jersey prevention of fraud law.
Also charged are Young and Alfred Williams, formerly a tax partner in the accountancy firm Touche Ross, now part of the international accountancy and consulting firm Deloitte Touche.
Touche Ross is also a party in the civil suit being brought against Cantrade by TTS and others.
The case relates to losses at several investment funds deposited with Cantrade by an outside fund management group. The investment funds were run on behalf of about 90 investors by TTS.

Cantrade said in its latest statement that its offer and a request for cooperation in communicating this offer to relevant investors, was made to the lawyer acting for the trustee, administrator and investment manager of TTS International SA.
"The offer is made on the express basis that Cantrade strongly denies any legal liability on its part, whether of civil or criminal nature," the statement also said.
Britain's Serious Fraud Office has said it is providing assistance to the Jersey authorities with regard to the alleged fraud. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
